cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-01.title: Coordinates are independent
cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-01.body:
The eight points at distance $\sqrt3$ are $(\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)$, and each step changes each coordinate by $\pm1$ independently with equal probability. After two steps each coordinate is $0$ (probability $\frac12$) or $\pm2$ (probability $\frac12$), independently.

The squared distance is $8$ exactly when the coordinates' squares are $0,4,4$ in some order (the only way to write $8$ as a sum of three squares of these values). Exactly one coordinate must be $0$: probability $3\cdot\left(\frac12\right)^3=\frac38$.

**Answer: $\frac38$**

cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-03.title: Row/column sets and L-shapes
cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-03.body:
A commutable set is a path of three squares: a straight line (a row or column of the grid) or an L-shape.

A partition cannot contain both a row set and a column set (they would meet), and every partition must contain at least one straight set (an L-tromino cannot be completed into a partition of the $3\times3$ grid with only L-shapes: the corner squares and the center cannot all be covered). If the middle row (or column) is a straight set, the other two rows (columns) are forced to be straight too, otherwise they cannot be tiled.

So the possibilities are:

- all three rows, or all three columns: $2$ partitions;
- an outer line (top row, bottom row, left column or right column) is a straight set and the remaining $2\times3$ block is split into two L-shapes, which can be done in $2$ ways: $4\cdot2=8$ partitions.

Total $2+8=10$. (A brute-force enumeration also gives $10$.)

**Answer: 10**

cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-04.title: Every lap looks the same
cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-04.body:
Consider the halfway point of any lap. If Dilhan arrives with the phone, he drops it with probability $\frac13$, so he keeps it with probability $\frac23$ (and does not drop it again that lap). If he arrives without it, the phone is on the ground at this point (he dropped it earlier at a halfway point), and he picks it up with probability $\frac23$.

So whether or not he started the lap with the phone, after the halfway point of the lap he has it with probability $\frac23$, and nothing else changes during the rest of the lap. After the halfway point of lap $12$ the probability is $\frac23$, and it stays so until the finish.

**Answer: $\frac23$**

cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-05.title: Inclusion-exclusion
cmimc-2022-combocs-d2-05.body:
**Zack reverse-sweeps Daniel.** Daniel wins $10$ rounds before Zack's first win, and Zack then reaches $11$; the game ends with Zack's $11$th win. Write the $21$ rounds won by Daniel or Zack: first $10$ D's, then $11$ Z's. Ethan's wins (at most $10$ of them, since Ethan never reaches $11$) are inserted anywhere before the last Z. Pad with extra E's after the last Z to make exactly $10$ E's; this is a bijection with arrangements of $21$ letters D/Z (in fixed order) and $10$ E's, so there are $\binom{31}{10}$ sequences.

**Zack reverse-sweeps Ethan.** By symmetry also $\binom{31}{10}$.

**Both.** Daniel and Ethan each reach $10$ before Zack's first win, then Zack wins $11$ in a row: the order of the $10$ D's and $10$ E's is arbitrary: $\binom{20}{10}$.

By inclusion-exclusion the total is $2\binom{31}{10}-\binom{20}{10}=2\cdot44352165-184756=88519574$. (The same count obtained by directly counting game sequences with a small program agrees, and so does the formula on smaller versions of the game.)

**Answer: $2\binom{31}{10}-\binom{20}{10}=88519574$**
